paraphrase: The true teaching has no sudden or gradual; people's natures are sharp or dull — the deluded cultivate gradually, the awakened accord suddenly. From the beginning this gate has taken no-thought as its tenet, no-form as its substance and non-abiding as its root: no-form is being amid forms yet free of forms; no-thought is being amid thoughts yet not thinking; non-abiding is the original nature of people. No-thought does not mean thinking of nothing: if every thought is cut off one dies and is reborn elsewhere — a great error. 'Thought' means thinking of suchness; suchness is the substance of thought and thought its function.

paraphrase: There are many ways into the Way but essentially two: entry by principle and entry by practice. Entry by principle is to awaken to the tenet through the teaching, deeply believing that all living beings share one true nature, covered by adventitious dust and deluded thought; if one abandons the false, returns to the true, and abides firmly in wall-gazing, self and other, ordinary and holy are one, one no longer follows the written teachings, and one is in silent accord with principle.

paraphrase: Though there are many gates into the Way, in essence they are two: sudden awakening and gradual cultivation. Even the 'sudden awakening, sudden cultivation' of the highest faculties rests on gradual cultivation in past lives; all sages first awaken, then cultivate, and through cultivation realise.
